task_description: Scrape product pricing from a React single-page application
failure_reason: Static HTTP requests cannot access content rendered by JavaScript frameworks. The response HTML is an empty shell with just a root div.
error_message: ResultSet is empty. No elements found matching selector '.price'
what_was_tried: Used requests.get() to fetch the page, then BeautifulSoup to parse price elements. Tried 4 different CSS selectors.
lesson: React, Vue, and Angular SPAs require browser automation. Static HTTP requests only return the empty HTML shell, not the rendered content.
suggested_approach: Use Playwright or Selenium with headless Chrome. Wait for the DOM to fully render before extracting elements.

task_description: Call OpenAI GPT-4 API with an entire 300-page PDF document
failure_reason: The input token count (128,000+) exceeded the model's context window limit. The API rejected the request before processing.
error_message: This model's maximum context length is 128000 tokens. Your messages resulted in 142381 tokens.
what_was_tried: Passed entire PDF text as a single user message to GPT-4.
lesson: Always check token count before sending to any LLM API. Large documents must be chunked or summarized first.
suggested_approach: Split document into 4000-token chunks with 200-token overlap. Process each chunk separately, then synthesize results.

task_description: Parse LangChain agent output into a structured JSON object
failure_reason: The LLM returned a mix of explanation text and JSON, but the output parser expected pure JSON only. The extra text broke JSON parsing.
error_message: Invalid json output: Sure! Here is the result: {"status": "complete"}. Got invalid JSON.
what_was_tried: Used LangChain's JsonOutputParser directly on raw LLM output.
lesson: LLMs often prepend explanation text before JSON output. Never parse raw LLM output directly — always extract JSON from within the response.
suggested_approach: Use json_repair library or regex to extract JSON block. Or add 'Return ONLY valid JSON, no explanation text' to system prompt. Or use structured outputs / function calling.

task_description: Connect to Pinecone vector database and query similar embeddings
failure_reason: API key was loaded from environment variables before the dotenv library initialized. The key was None at connection time.
error_message: PineconeException: API Key not provided. Pass API key as parameter or set PINECONE_API_KEY environment variable.
what_was_tried: Called pinecone.init() at module load time, before dotenv.load_dotenv() was called in main().
lesson: Always call dotenv.load_dotenv() before any code that reads environment variables. Module-level initialization runs before main().
suggested_approach: Move dotenv.load_dotenv() to the very top of your entry file, or use a lazy initialization pattern that reads env vars only when the function is called.

task_description: Run a LangGraph multi-agent pipeline with 5 sequential nodes
failure_reason: One agent node returned None instead of the expected state dict. LangGraph tried to merge None with the graph state, causing a crash.
error_message: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable at node 'analyzer_agent'
what_was_tried: Built a 5-node sequential LangGraph pipeline. The analyzer_agent node had a missing return statement in an if-else branch.
lesson: Every LangGraph node MUST return the full state dict in every code path. Missing return statements in conditional branches cause the graph to crash on that path.
suggested_approach: Add an explicit return statement in every if/elif/else branch. Use TypedDict for state to catch missing keys at development time.

task_description: Send automated WhatsApp messages via Twilio API
failure_reason: Twilio WhatsApp sandbox requires messages to be sent to numbers that have opted-in with a JOIN keyword. The recipient number had not joined the sandbox.
error_message: Error 63016: Channel could not authenticate. The recipient is not in your sandbox.
what_was_tried: Created Twilio client and sent message directly to phone number without sandbox opt-in.
lesson: Twilio WhatsApp sandbox requires recipients to opt-in by texting a JOIN keyword to the sandbox number. Production WhatsApp requires an approved Twilio business account.
suggested_approach: For testing: have recipient send JOIN [sandbox-keyword] to +1-415-523-8886. For production: apply for WhatsApp Business API approval through Twilio.

task_description: Use Claude API to generate structured tool call responses
failure_reason: Tool definitions were passed in the wrong format. The 'tools' parameter expects a list of dicts with a specific schema that was not followed.
error_message: 400 Bad Request: tools[0].input_schema is required and must be a valid JSON Schema object.
what_was_tried: Passed tool definitions with 'parameters' key instead of 'input_schema'. Used OpenAI tool format instead of Anthropic format.
lesson: Anthropic and OpenAI use different schemas for tool definitions. OpenAI uses 'parameters', Anthropic uses 'input_schema'. They are not interchangeable.
suggested_approach: Check Anthropic docs for exact tool schema format. Key fields: name, description, input_schema (with type: object, properties, required).

task_description: Implement a RAG pipeline with document chunking and Pinecone storage
failure_reason: All document chunks were given the same embedding ID, so each new upsert overwrote the previous one. Only the last chunk was stored.
error_message: No error thrown — silent data loss. Query returned only 1 result regardless of top_k value.
what_was_tried: Chunked document into 50 pieces, generated embeddings, upserted all with ID='doc_chunk'.
lesson: Pinecone upsert is an UPSERT — it overwrites existing vectors with the same ID. Every chunk needs a unique ID.
suggested_approach: Use f'doc_{document_id}_chunk_{i}' as the vector ID where i is the chunk index. Never reuse IDs across chunks.

task_description: Build a ReAct agent that browses the web and summarizes news articles
failure_reason: Agent entered an infinite loop — it kept calling the search tool repeatedly because it never evaluated whether the search results were sufficient to answer the question.
error_message: Agent stopped due to max_iterations=10. Last action was search_tool for the 10th consecutive time.
what_was_tried: Built ReAct agent with web search tool. Agent kept searching instead of reasoning on existing results.
lesson: ReAct agents need explicit stopping criteria. Without evaluation logic, they loop on the tool that produced the last relevant result.
suggested_approach: Add a 'have_enough_info' check after each tool call. Set max_iterations. Add an 'analyze_results' node before next tool call that decides if more search is needed.

task_description: Call external REST API from within a LangChain tool
failure_reason: The external API used OAuth2 Bearer token authentication. The agent sent an API key in a query parameter instead of the Authorization header.
error_message: 401 Unauthorized: Invalid authentication credentials.
what_was_tried: Passed API key as ?api_key=xxx query parameter. API requires Authorization: Bearer xxx header.
lesson: Always check the API's authentication method. OAuth2/Bearer token APIs require the Authorization header, not query parameters.
suggested_approach: Use headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}'} in requests.get(). Read the API documentation for the exact header format.

task_description: Extract structured data from a PDF invoice using an LLM
failure_reason: PyPDF2 extracted garbled text from a scanned (image-based) PDF. The PDF contained images of text, not actual text characters.
error_message: No actual error — extracted text was '\x00\x00\x00\x00' repeated. LLM returned 'I cannot find any invoice data in the provided text.'
what_was_tried: Used PyPDF2 to extract text, then passed to Claude for structured extraction. Text extraction returned binary garbage.
lesson: Scanned PDFs contain images, not text. Standard PDF text extraction libraries fail silently on image-based PDFs.
suggested_approach: Detect if PDF is image-based by checking if text extraction returns empty or garbage. If so, use OCR: pytesseract, Amazon Textract, or Google Document AI.

task_description: Store conversation history for a multi-turn chatbot using LangChain memory
failure_reason: ConversationBufferMemory was initialized inside the request handler function, creating a new memory object on every request. History was never persisted.
error_message: No error — chatbot simply forgot all previous messages on every new request.
what_was_tried: Created new ConversationBufferMemory() inside the /chat route handler for each API call.
lesson: In-memory objects reset on every function call. Memory must be initialized once (at app startup or per-user session) and stored externally between requests.
suggested_approach: Store memory in Redis or a database keyed by session/user ID. Use LangChain's RedisChatMessageHistory or PostgresChatMessageHistory for persistence.

task_description: Run async LangGraph pipeline inside a FastAPI endpoint
failure_reason: Used asyncio.run() inside an async FastAPI route handler. asyncio.run() creates a new event loop but FastAPI already has a running event loop, causing a conflict.
error_message: RuntimeError: This event loop is already running. Cannot run nested event loops.
what_was_tried: Called asyncio.run(graph.ainvoke(inputs)) inside an async def FastAPI route.
lesson: Never use asyncio.run() inside an already-running async context (FastAPI, Jupyter, etc.). Use await directly instead.
suggested_approach: Replace asyncio.run(graph.ainvoke(inputs)) with await graph.ainvoke(inputs) inside the async FastAPI route.

task_description: Use LangChain tool with Pydantic model for input validation
failure_reason: Pydantic v2 was installed but LangChain expected Pydantic v1 syntax. The BaseModel and validator decorators have breaking changes between versions.
error_message: ImportError: cannot import name 'validator' from 'pydantic'. Use 'field_validator' in Pydantic v2.
what_was_tried: Created StructuredTool with Pydantic BaseModel using @validator decorator (Pydantic v1 syntax).
lesson: LangChain version compatibility with Pydantic is critical. LangChain <0.2 uses Pydantic v1. LangChain >=0.2 supports Pydantic v2. Check your versions.
suggested_approach: Pin pydantic==1.10.x if using older LangChain, or upgrade to langchain>=0.2 and update validators to @field_validator with v2 syntax.

task_description: Generate embeddings for 10,000 documents and store in Pinecone
failure_reason: OpenAI embeddings API has a rate limit of 1,000,000 tokens per minute (TPM). Batch processing 10,000 documents simultaneously hit the rate limit after ~500 documents.
error_message: openai.RateLimitError: Rate limit reached for text-embedding-3-small. Try again in 30s.
what_was_tried: Generated embeddings for all 10,000 documents sequentially without any rate limit handling.
lesson: OpenAI embedding API has strict rate limits. Large batches will hit them. Always implement retry logic with exponential backoff.
suggested_approach: Use tenacity library for retries. Batch documents into groups of 100. Add time.sleep(0.1) between batches. Use OpenAI's official backoff: wait 2^n seconds on rate limit errors.

task_description: Build a code generation agent that writes and executes Python files
failure_reason: Agent generated code using f-strings with triple quotes that conflicted with the outer string delimiters, creating a syntax error in the written file.
error_message: SyntaxError: EOL while scanning string literal in generated_code.py line 23
what_was_tried: LLM generated Python code with nested triple-quote strings. When written to file, the quotes were not properly escaped.
lesson: LLM-generated code with string literals inside strings causes escaping conflicts. Code generation agents must validate syntax before execution.
suggested_approach: Run ast.parse(generated_code) before writing to file. If it raises SyntaxError, send the error back to the LLM for correction. Add a 3-attempt retry loop.

task_description: Use FAISS local vector store instead of Pinecone for document retrieval
failure_reason: FAISS index was rebuilt from scratch on every application restart because the index was not saved to disk. All embeddings were lost between restarts.
error_message: No error — index was empty on restart, returning no results for all queries.
what_was_tried: Built FAISS index in memory, queried it successfully. After restarting the server, index was empty.
lesson: FAISS is an in-memory index. It does not persist automatically. You must explicitly save it to disk after building and load it on startup.
suggested_approach: Call vectorstore.save_local('faiss_index') after building. Call FAISS.load_local('faiss_index', embeddings) on startup. Check if the directory exists before deciding to rebuild.

task_description: Web scraping agent that handles pagination across 50 pages
failure_reason: Website implemented bot detection. After page 3, the site started returning CAPTCHA pages and eventually blocked the IP address.
error_message: No error raised — responses had status 200 but HTML contained 'Please verify you are human' instead of data.
what_was_tried: Scraped pages sequentially with no delay, using default Python requests headers.
lesson: Aggressive scraping triggers bot detection. Websites check request frequency, User-Agent headers, and request patterns.
suggested_approach: Add random delays (2-5 seconds) between requests. Set realistic User-Agent headers. Use rotating proxies. Respect robots.txt. Consider official APIs if available.

task_description: Implement streaming responses from Claude API in a FastAPI endpoint
failure_reason: Used regular anthropic.messages.create() instead of the streaming variant. The entire response was buffered before being sent, defeating the purpose of streaming.
error_message: No error — API worked, but client received the full response all at once after a long wait instead of token-by-token.
what_was_tried: Set stream=True on regular messages.create() call. Wrapped response in FastAPI StreamingResponse.
lesson: Anthropic streaming requires using the context manager API: with client.messages.stream() as stream. The stream=True flag alone is not sufficient for proper streaming.
suggested_approach: Use: with anthropic.Anthropic().messages.stream(...) as stream: for text in stream.text_stream: yield text. Wrap in FastAPI's StreamingResponse with media_type='text/event-stream'.

task_description: Normalize and validate user profile data before passing to downstream agent
failure_reason: User submitted profile with unexpected null fields. The next agent assumed all fields were present and crashed when trying to access email.lower() on a None value.
error_message: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower'
what_was_tried: Passed raw user input dict directly to next agent without field validation.
lesson: Always validate and normalize data at agent handoff boundaries. Never assume upstream data is complete or correctly typed.
suggested_approach: Define a Pydantic model with Optional fields and default values for all inter-agent data contracts. Validate at every handoff. Log the raw input before validation for debugging.

task_description: Build a Slack bot that responds to messages using Claude
failure_reason: Slack sends duplicate events when the bot does not acknowledge the event within 3 seconds. The bot was calling Claude (slow) before acknowledging, causing duplicate responses.
error_message: No error — bot sent the same message 2-3 times per user message.
what_was_tried: Called Claude API synchronously inside the Slack event handler before calling ack().
lesson: Slack requires event acknowledgment within 3 seconds or it retries the event. Always call ack() immediately, then process asynchronously.
suggested_approach: Call ack() first, then spawn an async task or thread to call Claude and post the response. Use Slack Bolt's async app with asyncio for clean async handling.

task_description: Query a database and pass results to an LLM for natural language analysis
failure_reason: SQL query returned 50,000 rows of raw data. When serialized to string and passed to the LLM, it exceeded the context window limit.
error_message: Error code 400: max_tokens is too large. The prompt is 189,234 tokens which exceeds the model maximum of 128,000.
what_was_tried: Fetched all rows from database table, converted to CSV string, passed entire string to LLM for analysis.
lesson: Raw database results are almost never suitable for direct LLM consumption. Aggregate, filter, or paginate first.
suggested_approach: Pre-aggregate data in SQL before fetching. Use GROUP BY, COUNT, AVG etc. Pass summary statistics, not raw rows. Or implement Text-to-SQL where LLM writes the SQL query itself.

task_description: Deploy FastAPI backend with LangGraph agent to Railway
failure_reason: Application worked locally but crashed immediately on Railway. The Procfile started uvicorn without the --host 0.0.0.0 flag, causing Railway's health check to fail.
error_message: Error: Health check failed. The service is not responding on port 8000.
what_was_tried: Deployed with Procfile: web: uvicorn main:app --port 8000. Railway health check could not reach the service.
lesson: Cloud deployments require the server to bind to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces), not localhost. Binding to localhost only exposes the port inside the container.
suggested_approach: Use: web: uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT. Railway injects the PORT environment variable — use it instead of hardcoding 8000.

task_description: Implement multi-agent workflow where agents share data through a queue
failure_reason: Python's standard Queue was used in a multi-threaded setup, but one agent was async and one was sync. The async agent's event loop blocked waiting for the queue in a sync context.
error_message: Application hung indefinitely. No error raised. Queue.get() blocked the async event loop.
what_was_tried: Mixed asyncio agents and threading-based agents sharing a single queue.Queue instance.
lesson: Never mix queue.Queue (threading) with asyncio in the same application. They operate on different concurrency models and will deadlock.
suggested_approach: Use asyncio.Queue for async agents. Use queue.Queue for threaded agents. Never mix them. If you must bridge async and sync code, use asyncio.run_in_executor().

task_description: Use LangGraph conditional edges to route between different specialist agents
failure_reason: Conditional edge function returned a string that didn't match any registered edge destination. LangGraph silently routed to END instead of the intended agent.
error_message: No error — graph completed successfully but skipped the intended specialist agent entirely.
what_was_tried: Conditional function returned 'finance_agent' but the edge map had the key 'financial_agent'. Case and spelling mismatch.
lesson: LangGraph conditional edges silently route to END on unrecognized return values. Always use constants or Enum for edge routing keys. Test every routing path explicitly.
suggested_approach: Define routing keys as constants: ROUTE_FINANCE = 'financial_agent'. Use the constant in both the conditional function and the edge map. Add an 'else: raise ValueError' in your conditional function for unmapped routes.

task_description: Send emails automatically using an AI agent via Gmail SMTP
failure_reason: Google blocked SMTP access with a regular Gmail password. Google requires App Passwords or OAuth2 for programmatic email access.
error_message: smtplib.SMTPAuthenticationError: (535, b'5.7.8 Username and Password not accepted. Learn more at https://support.google.com/mail/?p=BadCredentials')
what_was_tried: Used Gmail address and account password directly in smtplib connection.
lesson: Google disabled less-secure app access. Gmail SMTP requires either a 16-character App Password (with 2FA enabled) or OAuth2 authentication.
suggested_approach: Enable 2-Factor Authentication on Google account. Generate an App Password under Security settings. Use the App Password (not account password) in smtplib. Or use Google's official Gmail API with OAuth2.

task_description: Agent that reads GitHub issues and auto-generates pull request descriptions
failure_reason: GitHub API token had read-only scope. The agent could read issues but failed when trying to create/update pull requests which requires write scope.
error_message: github.GithubException.GithubException: 403 {'message': 'Resource not accessible by personal access token', 'status': '403'}
what_was_tried: Created GitHub Personal Access Token with 'repo:read' scope. Attempted to create PR with write operations.
lesson: GitHub Personal Access Tokens have granular scopes. Read and write are separate permissions. Always create tokens with the minimum required scope.
suggested_approach: Create a new PAT with 'repo' scope (full control of private repos) or 'public_repo' for public repos. Store in environment variables, never hardcode.

task_description: Process uploaded CSV file in a LangChain agent tool
failure_reason: CSV file used semicolons as delimiters but pandas read_csv() defaults to comma. All data was read into a single column.
error_message: No error — dataframe had 1 column instead of 8. All analysis returned incorrect results silently.
what_was_tried: Called pd.read_csv(file_path) without specifying separator. File was semicolon-delimited.
lesson: Always detect or specify CSV delimiter. European CSVs often use semicolons. Never assume comma delimiters.
suggested_approach: Use pd.read_csv(file, sep=None, engine='python') to auto-detect separator. Or check the first line of the file and detect delimiter before reading.

task_description: Implement tool calling with OpenAI function calling API
failure_reason: Tool function returned a Python dict object, but OpenAI expects tool results to be strings. The dict was converted to Python repr format, not JSON, confusing the model.
error_message: No error — model received tool result as "{'status': 'ok', 'data': [...]}" (Python repr) and could not parse it correctly.
what_was_tried: Returned Python dict from tool function. OpenAI automatically called str() on it instead of json.dumps().
lesson: OpenAI tool results must be strings. Always serialize dict results with json.dumps(), not str() or repr().
suggested_approach: Return json.dumps(result_dict) from tool functions. This ensures valid JSON formatting that the model can reliably parse.

task_description: Build a document Q&A agent using RAG with PDF source documents
failure_reason: Documents were chunked at fixed 1000-character boundaries, splitting sentences and even words in the middle. The resulting chunks were semantically incomplete and retrieval quality was poor.
error_message: No error — agent gave vague, incorrect answers. Retrieved chunks started/ended mid-sentence.
what_was_tried: Used CharacterTextSplitter with chunk_size=1000, chunk_overlap=0. Chunks broke mid-sentence.
lesson: Fixed character chunking ignores semantic boundaries. Chunks that break mid-sentence produce poor embeddings and low retrieval quality.
suggested_approach: Use RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter which respects paragraph, sentence, and word boundaries. Add chunk_overlap=200 to maintain context at boundaries. Or use semantic chunking based on sentence embeddings.

task_description: Scrape and monitor a website for price changes every 5 minutes
failure_reason: The scheduler ran the scraping function correctly but the function made synchronous requests inside an async scheduler. The event loop blocked on each request.
error_message: No error — scheduler ran but each job took 60+ seconds instead of 2 seconds, causing jobs to pile up.
what_was_tried: Used APScheduler's AsyncIOScheduler but called synchronous requests.get() inside the async job function.
lesson: Synchronous I/O inside async functions blocks the entire event loop. All other async tasks freeze until the sync call completes.
suggested_approach: Replace requests with httpx.AsyncClient and use await client.get(). Or run sync code in a thread: await asyncio.run_in_executor(None, requests.get, url).

task_description: Use Anthropic Claude to classify customer support tickets into categories
failure_reason: Prompt asked Claude to return one of 5 category names, but Claude sometimes returned category names with different capitalization or added punctuation like periods.
error_message: No error — classifier returned 'Billing.' instead of 'BILLING', causing downstream category matching to fail silently.
what_was_tried: Asked Claude to return one of: BILLING, TECHNICAL, SHIPPING, RETURNS, OTHER. Claude returned 'Billing.' with inconsistent casing.
lesson: LLMs do not guarantee exact string matching even when given explicit options. Always normalize or post-process LLM categorical outputs.
suggested_approach: Post-process: output.strip().upper().rstrip('.,'). Or use structured outputs / tool calling where the category is a constrained enum field. Or use few-shot examples showing exact output format.

task_description: Build an agent that automatically creates Notion pages with research summaries
failure_reason: Notion API requires content to be broken into blocks with specific types. Agent tried to pass a plain text string as page content, which the API rejected.
error_message: APIResponseError: body failed validation. body.children[0].type should be one of: paragraph, heading_1, heading_2...
what_was_tried: Passed {'content': 'Summary text here...'} as the page children parameter.
lesson: Notion API uses a block-based content model. Every piece of content must be structured as a block with type, and text must be wrapped in rich_text arrays.
suggested_approach: Structure content as: [{'object': 'block', 'type': 'paragraph', 'paragraph': {'rich_text': [{'type': 'text', 'text': {'content': text}}]}}]. Build a helper function that converts plain text to Notion blocks.

task_description: Implement agent memory using LangChain's ConversationSummaryMemory
failure_reason: Summary memory called the LLM API to generate a summary on every single message, including short one-word responses. API costs exploded and latency doubled.
error_message: No error — memory worked correctly but made 2x API calls per message. Monthly cost tripled.
what_was_tried: Used ConversationSummaryMemory as drop-in replacement for ConversationBufferMemory.
lesson: ConversationSummaryMemory calls the LLM to summarize after every message exchange. This doubles API calls. Use it only when conversation exceeds token limits.
suggested_approach: Use ConversationBufferMemory for short conversations. Switch to ConversationSummaryBufferMemory with max_token_limit=2000, which only summarizes when the buffer exceeds the limit.

task_description: Agent that monitors and processes files uploaded to an S3 bucket
failure_reason: S3 event trigger fired correctly but the Lambda function processing it timed out because the LLM API call took longer than the default 3-second Lambda timeout.
error_message: Task timed out after 3.00 seconds
what_was_tried: Called Claude API synchronously inside Lambda function with default 3-second timeout.
lesson: LLM API calls typically take 5-30 seconds. Default Lambda timeout (3s) is insufficient. Always set appropriate timeouts for AI workloads.
suggested_approach: Set Lambda timeout to at least 60 seconds for LLM calls, 300 seconds for complex agent pipelines. Use async Lambda invocation for long-running tasks. Set LLM max_tokens appropriately to control response time.

task_description: Parse and extract data from deeply nested JSON API response
failure_reason: Agent assumed consistent JSON structure but the API sometimes omitted optional nested keys. KeyError on missing keys crashed the agent mid-pipeline.
error_message: KeyError: 'metadata' at response['data']['results'][0]['metadata']['created_at']
what_was_tried: Used direct dictionary key access for deeply nested JSON without any null checks.
lesson: API responses are not guaranteed to have all keys present, especially optional fields. Never use direct key access on external API data without defensive coding.
suggested_approach: Use dict.get() with default values: response.get('data', {}).get('results', [{}])[0].get('metadata', {}).get('created_at'). Or use pydantic with Optional fields to deserialize safely.

task_description: Build a multi-agent system where a planner assigns tasks to specialist agents
failure_reason: Planner agent generated task assignments as free-form text. The task parser used substring matching to extract assignments, which failed when the planner used slightly different phrasing.
error_message: No error — planner said 'assign to financial_specialist' but parser looked for 'ASSIGN: financial_agent'. 0 tasks were dispatched.
what_was_tried: Used regex pattern matching on planner output text to extract agent assignments.
lesson: Free-text task assignment parsing is brittle. Any variation in LLM phrasing breaks the parser. Use structured outputs for inter-agent communication.
suggested_approach: Define a TaskAssignment Pydantic model. Use structured output / tool calling to force the planner to output valid TaskAssignment objects. Never parse agent-to-agent communication with regex.

task_description: Process and analyze uploaded images using Claude vision capabilities
failure_reason: Images were passed as file paths (strings) instead of base64-encoded data. Claude API requires images to be either base64-encoded or accessible URLs.
error_message: anthropic.BadRequestError: 400 Bad Request: image source type 'file_path' is not supported. Use 'base64' or 'url'.
what_was_tried: Passed local file path '/tmp/image.jpg' as the image source in the API call.
lesson: Claude and most vision APIs do not accept local file paths. Images must be base64-encoded or hosted at a public URL.
suggested_approach: Read file and encode: with open(path, 'rb') as f: data = base64.standard_b64encode(f.read()).decode('utf-8'). Then pass as {'type': 'base64', 'media_type': 'image/jpeg', 'data': data}.

task_description: Build an agent that writes code and runs it in a sandboxed Python environment
failure_reason: Agent-generated code imported the 'os' module and used os.system() to execute shell commands, breaking out of the intended Python sandbox.
error_message: No error — agent successfully ran system commands including file deletion outside the sandbox directory.
what_was_tried: Used Python's exec() to run generated code without import restrictions.
lesson: exec() without restrictions allows full system access including os.system(), subprocess, and file operations. Never use bare exec() for untrusted LLM-generated code.
suggested_approach: Use RestrictedPython or run code in a Docker container with limited permissions. Block dangerous modules: os, sys, subprocess, importlib. Or use E2B's sandboxed code execution API.

task_description: Create a vector similarity search across millions of documents
failure_reason: Pinecone free tier has a limit of 100,000 vectors per index. Attempting to upsert beyond this limit caused silent failures where vectors were dropped.
error_message: No error thrown — upsert returned success but vectors were silently dropped after reaching the 100k limit.
what_was_tried: Inserted 500,000 vectors into a free-tier Pinecone index.
lesson: Pinecone free tier limits: 1 index, 100,000 vectors, 1,536 dimensions. Exceeding limits causes silent drops without error. Check plan limits before designing your pipeline.
suggested_approach: Upgrade to Pinecone Starter ($70/month) for unlimited vectors, or use Weaviate/Qdrant self-hosted for free unlimited storage. Monitor vector count with describe_index_stats().

task_description: Use a web search tool inside a LangChain agent
failure_reason: SerpAPI key was valid but the free tier limited to 100 searches/month. Key expired mid-pipeline during a large batch processing job.
error_message: serpapi.GoogleSearchException: This account has reached its search limit. Upgrade your plan at serpapi.com.
what_was_tried: Used SerpAPI for web search tool in production LangChain agent without monitoring usage.
lesson: Free API tiers have strict usage limits. Always monitor API usage and implement quota checks before long-running batch operations.
suggested_approach: Switch to Tavily Search API (better LangChain integration, generous free tier). Or use DuckDuckGo search (free, no API key): from langchain_community.tools import DuckDuckGoSearchRun.

task_description: Stream responses from a LangGraph agent to a Next.js frontend
failure_reason: CORS policy blocked the WebSocket connection from the Next.js frontend (localhost:3000) to the FastAPI backend (localhost:8000). Browser refused the connection.
error_message: WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost:8000/ws' failed: Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 403
what_was_tried: Created WebSocket endpoint in FastAPI without CORS configuration. Connected from Next.js frontend.
lesson: FastAPI does not automatically allow cross-origin WebSocket connections. CORS must be configured to allow the frontend origin.
suggested_approach: Add to FastAPI: app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=['http://localhost:3000'], allow_credentials=True). WebSocket connections also need origin validation.

task_description: Agent that generates and sends marketing emails to a customer list
failure_reason: Agent sent 5,000 emails without any rate limiting. Gmail SMTP server blocked the account after the first 500 emails, and the remaining 4,500 were silently dropped.
error_message: smtplib.SMTPException: (421, b'4.7.0 Try again later, closing connection.')
what_was_tried: Looped through all 5,000 email addresses and sent emails sequentially as fast as possible.
lesson: Email providers enforce strict rate limits. Gmail: 500/day for personal, 2,000/day for Workspace. Exceeding limits causes account suspension.
suggested_approach: Use a transactional email service: SendGrid, Mailgun, or AWS SES — they handle rate limiting, bounces, and unsubscribes automatically. Add delays between sends and track delivery status.

task_description: Fine-tune prompt to make an agent always respond in valid JSON
failure_reason: Prompt said 'respond in JSON format' but the LLM added markdown code blocks (```json ... ```) around the JSON. The json.loads() call failed on the backtick wrapper.
error_message: json.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) at '```json\n{...}'
what_was_tried: Added 'Respond in JSON format' to system prompt. Called json.loads() directly on response text.
lesson: LLMs often wrap JSON in markdown code blocks even when asked for plain JSON. Always strip code block markers before parsing.
suggested_approach: Strip markers: text.strip().lstrip('```json').lstrip('```').rstrip('```').strip(). Or use regex: re.search(r'\{.*\}', text, re.DOTALL). Or use Anthropic's structured output feature.

task_description: Implement human-in-the-loop approval for LangGraph agent actions
failure_reason: LangGraph interrupt() was called to pause the graph and wait for human approval, but the graph state was stored in-memory. After the approval endpoint was called, the graph had no state to resume from.
error_message: ValueError: Cannot resume graph: checkpoint not found for thread_id 'thread_abc123'
what_was_tried: Used MemorySaver (in-memory checkpointer) for graph state. Server restarted between interrupt and resume calls.
lesson: MemorySaver stores state in RAM only. Human-in-the-loop workflows require durable state that survives server restarts.
suggested_approach: Use SqliteSaver or PostgresSaver for durable checkpointing. State persists across restarts. Use thread_id to identify and resume specific graph runs.

task_description: Build an agent that summarizes YouTube video transcripts
failure_reason: youtube_transcript_api failed on videos where the creator disabled transcripts or where auto-generated captions were not available in English.
error_message: youtube_transcript_api.CouldNotRetrieveTranscript: Could not retrieve a transcript for the video https://youtube.com/watch?v=xxx. Subtitles are disabled for this video.
what_was_tried: Called YouTubeTranscriptApi.get_transcript(video_id) without fallback handling.
lesson: YouTube transcript availability is not guaranteed. Many videos have transcripts disabled or unavailable in the target language.
suggested_approach: Wrap in try/except TranscriptsDisabledError. Try multiple languages: get_transcript(id, languages=['en', 'en-US', 'en-GB']). As fallback, use Whisper to transcribe the audio if transcript unavailable.

task_description: Create a LangChain agent with multiple tools and ReAct prompting
failure_reason: Agent was given 15 different tools. The tool selection reasoning started failing because the prompt grew too long and the model started randomly selecting tools instead of the correct ones.
error_message: No error — agent selected wrong tools for tasks it previously handled correctly. Accuracy dropped from 92% to 61%.
what_was_tried: Registered all 15 tools with the ReAct agent at once.
lesson: Too many tools degrades LLM tool selection accuracy. Research shows performance degrades significantly beyond 10 tools in a single agent.
suggested_approach: Use tool routing: a lightweight router agent selects the top 3-5 relevant tools, then a specialist agent uses only those. Or group tools into specialist agents (search_agent, code_agent, data_agent) and route between them.

task_description: Implement webhook receiver for GitHub Actions CI notifications
failure_reason: GitHub webhook sent events with a signature header for HMAC verification. The agent did not validate the signature and GitHub eventually disabled the webhook after detecting no validation.
error_message: No error initially — webhook worked. GitHub disabled delivery after 72 hours of signature validation failures.
what_was_tried: Created webhook endpoint without implementing X-Hub-Signature-256 header validation.
lesson: GitHub webhooks include HMAC-SHA256 signatures for security verification. Not validating them is a security risk and GitHub may disable unvalidated webhooks.
suggested_approach: Validate signature: hmac.compare_digest(expected_sig, received_sig) where expected = 'sha256=' + hmac.new(secret, payload, sha256).hexdigest(). Reject requests with invalid signatures with 401.

task_description: Agent that reads and writes to a shared SQLite database concurrently
failure_reason: Multiple async agent workers tried to write to the same SQLite database simultaneously. SQLite's single-writer model caused database locking errors under concurrent load.
error_message: sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (sqlite3.OperationalError) database is locked
what_was_tried: Ran 5 parallel async agent workers all writing to the same SQLite file.
lesson: SQLite only supports one writer at a time. Concurrent multi-agent systems should use PostgreSQL or implement a write queue.
suggested_approach: Use PostgreSQL for concurrent write access. Or serialize writes through a single async queue: asyncio.Queue() with one DB writer worker consuming from it. Or use SQLite WAL mode for better concurrent reads.

task_description: Build a document comparison agent that identifies differences between two contracts
failure_reason: Both contracts were passed in a single prompt. At 40 pages each, the combined prompt exceeded context window. Only the first contract was analyzed because the second was truncated.
error_message: No error — agent returned analysis of only the first document. Second document was silently truncated from context.
what_was_tried: Concatenated both contract texts into a single message and asked Claude to compare them.
lesson: Very long contexts lead to 'lost in the middle' problem where LLMs lose attention to content in the middle of the context. Critical documents may be ignored.
suggested_approach: Implement map-reduce: extract key clauses from each document separately, then compare the extracted clauses. Or use document chunking with cross-referencing between chunks from each document.

task_description: Implement retry logic for failed LLM API calls
failure_reason: Retry logic retried immediately on RateLimitError without any backoff. This made rate limiting worse by sending more requests exactly when the API was overloaded.
error_message: openai.RateLimitError repeated 10 times in 1 second. Application eventually crashed.
what_was_tried: Used a for loop: for attempt in range(10): try: call_api() except: continue
lesson: Immediate retries on rate limit errors make the problem worse. Always use exponential backoff with jitter.
suggested_approach: Use tenacity: @retry(wait=wait_exponential(min=1, max=60), stop=stop_after_attempt(5), retry=retry_if_exception_type(RateLimitError)). Or use the official backoff library with exponential + jitter.

task_description: Agent that generates Python code and saves it to a Git repository
failure_reason: Agent pushed code directly to main branch without creating a pull request. In protected repository configurations, direct pushes to main are blocked.
error_message: remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main. Required status checks have not passed.
what_was_tried: Used GitPython to commit and push directly to main branch.
lesson: Production repositories protect main branch from direct pushes. Agents must create branches and pull requests, not push directly to main.
suggested_approach: Create a feature branch: repo.create_head(f'agent/{task_id}'). Commit to feature branch. Use GitHub API to create a pull request to main. Never push directly to protected branches.

task_description: Run a LangChain agent that processes user queries about a knowledge base
failure_reason: System prompt was 3,000 tokens long with extensive instructions. This left very little room in the context window for conversation history and retrieved documents, causing relevant context to be dropped.
error_message: No error — agent worked but gave incomplete answers because retrieved context was truncated to fit within context window.
what_was_tried: Wrote a very detailed 3,000-token system prompt with all instructions. Combined with conversation history and retrieved docs, context exceeded limit.
lesson: Every token in your system prompt reduces space for documents and conversation. Verbose system prompts degrade RAG quality.
suggested_approach: Keep system prompts under 500 tokens. Move detailed instructions to retrieved document metadata. Use prompt compression techniques like LLMLingua for very long contexts.

task_description: Deploy a LangGraph agent as a Docker container on AWS ECS
failure_reason: Docker image was built on an Apple M2 (ARM64) machine. When deployed to ECS which runs AMD64/x86_64 instances, the container failed to start because of architecture mismatch.
error_message: exec /usr/local/bin/python3: exec format error. Container failed to start.
what_was_tried: Built Docker image with docker build . on M2 Mac. Pushed to ECR. Deployed to ECS t3.medium instance.
lesson: Docker images built on Apple Silicon (ARM64) are not compatible with x86_64 cloud instances by default.
suggested_approach: Build multi-architecture images: docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t your-image . Or specify platform explicitly: docker build --platform linux/amd64 .

task_description: Implement a chatbot that maintains context across a 50-message conversation
failure_reason: After 20 messages, the full conversation history + system prompt exceeded the model's context window. New messages started replacing the beginning of the conversation, losing critical early context.
error_message: No error — model started giving inconsistent answers that contradicted earlier parts of the conversation after message 20.
what_was_tried: Kept full conversation in ConversationBufferMemory. Passed all messages on every turn.
lesson: Conversations grow unboundedly. Buffer memory without limits will eventually exceed context window, causing silent context loss.
suggested_approach: Use ConversationBufferWindowMemory(k=10) to keep only the last 10 exchanges. Or implement rolling summarization: summarize older messages, keep recent ones verbatim. Implement a 'conversation summary' that gets updated every 5 messages.

task_description: Process real-time stock data and generate trading signals using an AI agent
failure_reason: Agent used LLM to make individual decisions per stock tick, resulting in 100+ API calls per second. API costs reached $500 in the first hour.
error_message: No error — agent worked correctly. Monthly bill projection was $360,000.
what_was_tried: Called LLM for every incoming price tick to decide buy/sell/hold.
lesson: LLM calls cost money. Using them for high-frequency decisions on real-time data streams creates unsustainable costs. Use LLMs for high-level strategy, not per-tick decisions.
suggested_approach: Use LLM only for strategy generation (once per day or major market event). Implement the actual buy/sell logic with fast, cheap rule-based systems or traditional ML models for per-tick decisions.

task_description: Build an AI agent that writes unit tests for existing Python code
failure_reason: Agent generated test functions with names that did not start with 'test_'. pytest ignored all generated tests without raising any errors.
error_message: No error — pytest ran successfully: '0 tests collected'. All generated test functions were named 'check_*' instead of 'test_*'.
what_was_tried: Asked LLM to generate tests. LLM generated functions named check_login(), verify_output() etc. pytest only discovers functions named test_*.
lesson: pytest only collects test functions that start with 'test_' by default. Always validate test naming conventions after generation.
suggested_approach: Add explicit instruction: 'All test function names MUST start with test_ (e.g., test_login, test_output)'. Validate generated tests with ast.parse() and check function names before writing to file.

task_description: Use LangChain to summarize a news article from a URL
failure_reason: The target website used JavaScript to dynamically load article content. The URL loader fetched the static HTML which only contained navigation and ads, not the article text.
error_message: No error — LLM received empty article content and returned 'I cannot summarize this as no article content was provided.'
what_was_tried: Used WebBaseLoader to load URL. Website loaded article content via JavaScript after page load.
lesson: WebBaseLoader uses requests library which only fetches static HTML. JavaScript-rendered content is not captured.
suggested_approach: Use SeleniumURLLoader or PlaywrightURLLoader from LangChain for JavaScript-heavy sites. Or use a headless browser: browser.goto(url); browser.wait_for_selector('.article-body').

task_description: Build an agent pipeline where output of one LLM feeds as input to another
failure_reason: First LLM generated a response with 4,000 tokens. This was passed entirely as context to the second LLM, which combined with its own system prompt, exceeded the context window.
error_message: anthropic.BadRequestError: 400 prompt is too long: 138,921 tokens > 100,000 token limit
what_was_tried: Chained two LLM calls where first output fed directly as second input without size management.
lesson: Chaining LLM outputs creates compounding context growth. Each chain link can multiply token usage. Always constrain output size and summarize between chains.
suggested_approach: Set max_tokens on intermediate LLM calls to limit output size. Add a compression/summarization step between chains. Only pass relevant extracted sections to next agent, not full output.

task_description: Monitor a Postgres database for new records and trigger agent workflows
failure_reason: Agent used polling (SELECT * WHERE created_at > last_checked) every second. Under high load, the polling itself became a significant database load, slowing down the main application.
error_message: No error — polling worked but caused 30% increase in database CPU usage under load.
what_was_tried: Ran SELECT query every second from asyncio loop to check for new records.
lesson: Polling databases creates constant load regardless of whether new data exists. Use database change notifications for event-driven architectures.
suggested_approach: Use PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY: execute NOTIFY channel, 'new_record' on insert trigger. Agent listens with await conn.add_listener('channel', callback). Zero overhead when idle.

task_description: Implement LangGraph agent with tool calling that modifies external state
failure_reason: Agent called a tool that deleted a production database record. When the tool call result was wrong and the agent was re-run to fix the error, the deletion could not be undone.
error_message: No error — tool succeeded. Production data was permanently deleted. Agent re-run could not recover the data.
what_was_tried: Gave agent a tool with direct DELETE access to production database. Agent incorrectly identified a record for deletion.
lesson: AI agents should never have direct access to irreversible production actions (delete, send email to customers, charge payment). Always implement human-in-the-loop or reversible actions.
suggested_approach: Implement soft-delete: mark records as deleted=True instead of actually deleting. Add human approval step before irreversible actions using LangGraph interrupt(). Log all agent actions with full context for audit trail.
